title: Desires are beginningless (4.10–4.11)
hook: you can't find the first craving, and Patanjali says you don't need to
tomorrow: The object exists independent of the mind (4.14–4.17)

segments.voice: Yesterday: ashukla-akrishna, action neither white nor black, done free of its fruit.

It's eleven at night and you're standing at the open fridge, not hungry, looking for something. Or scrolling, thumb moving on its own. A familiar question shows up: why am I like this? When did this start? Childhood, a hard year, something someone said? We dig for the first cause as if finding it would switch the whole thing off. Patanjali's answer is short, almost blunt. There is no first one.
screen: `ELEVEN AT NIGHT, AT THE OPEN FRIDGE.` → `WHEN DID THIS START?` → `THERE IS NO FIRST ONE.`

segments.voice: Sutra 4.10: tasam anaditvam chashisho nityatvat. And they have no beginning, because the will to live is everlasting. They are the vasanas, the deep traces of desire laid down by past action. The commentary points to something anyone can see: every creature, from its first breath, wants to go on. Let me not stop being. That wish has no start date, so the traces it lays down have none either. If there's no first craving, there's no one moment to blame, and no point spending years in the archive. Then sutra 4.11 turns the key. These traces are held together by four things: a cause, a result, a place to rest in the mind, and an object to lean on. Take those away and the traces go too. A campfire can burn for as long as anyone remembers, and nobody knows who lit it. It still goes out when the wood stops coming. So the practice isn't archaeology. It's noticing what feeds the craving right now. Now the week, from the top. Omniscience offered, and the gods' invitation refused. Discernment down to the instant. Kaivalya, when the mind's purity equals the self's. The five sources of powers. The farmer opening the channel. Action neither white nor black. And today: desires without a beginning, which can still have an end.
screen: `THE WILL TO LIVE HAS NO START DATE.` · `NO FIRST CRAVING TO BLAME.` · `HELD BY FOUR SUPPORTS.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `TĀSĀM ANĀDITVAṂ CĀŚIṢO NITYATVĀT.`

segments.voice: Let a small want come up on its own: to check the phone, to shift, to get up. Don't ask where it came from; ask what it's leaning on right now, a thought, a sound, an itch, and name it quietly. Then watch what the want does once it's seen.
Vasana, the trace desire leaves behind. These traces have no first moment, because the will to live has none, but they rest on supports, and without them they fall away.
Your line: no beginning. But even a very old fire still needs wood. A week, done.

screen: `DAY 483 COUNTS.` → `ANOTHER WEEK OF PATANJALI, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: THE OBJECT EXISTS INDEPENDENT OF THE MIND.`

howItsDone: In the yoga tradition, vasanas are worked with less by searching for their origin than by withdrawing what sustains them: practice, non-attachment and discernment, as the earlier chapters of the Yoga Sutras teach.

match.prompt: what holds the traces together — tap the pairs.
pairs: the wish to go on living

myth: Patanjali says you must find the first desire to be free of it
4.10 says there is no first one; 4.11 says remove what supports the traces.
beginningless does not mean endless here
the traces have no start, but without their four supports they disappear.
the commentary links the traces to the wish to go on living
every creature wants to keep being, and that wish has no start date.

fork.setup: an old habit keeps coming back. following 4.10 and 4.11, where do you put your effort?
options: trace it back to the very first time.
remove what is feeding it now.
wait for it to wear itself out.
fork.reveal: the traces have no first moment to find, but they rest on cause, result, a resting place and an object. take those away, and the traces go.

original.note: Sanskrit vāsanā: a lingering trace or scent, the deep impression desire leaves behind.

trapdoor: what you thought: if I find where a craving began, it will stop.
what it means: the traces of desire have no first moment, but they need supports, and they fall away without them.
what a scholar hears: 4.11 names hetu, phala, ashraya and alambana, cause, fruit, substrate and object; the beginninglessness of 4.10 rests on ashis, the wish to be, close to abhinivesha in 2.9.
recall: mastery: a mind steady on anything
guess: a deep trace of desire, laid down by past action
a craving that began in one moment of childhood
a breath practice that burns away old desire

chat.says: If my cravings have no beginning, does that mean I'm stuck with them forever?
options: No. They have no first moment, but they rest on supports; without those, they fade.
Yes. With no beginning they can't ever end; you just learn to live with them.
No. Find the exact moment they began, and that memory will switch them off.
chat.meaning: Sutra 4.10: the traces have no beginning. Sutra 4.11: they rest on a cause, a result, a resting place and an object. Remove those, and they go.

vasana.meaning: a deep trace of desire laid down by past action

Kaivalya.meaning: freedom: the seer standing alone, untangled from the mind

sources.ref: Yoga Sutra 4.11 (cause, result, substrate and object hold the traces)
Yoga Sutra 4.10, Vyasa's commentary (the wish to go on being, in every creature)
